document_metadata.main_location: DAN PIENAAR SECONDARY SCHOOL FOR BOYS
document_metadata.summary: At a Johannesburg school, Jonathan is tripped by a student, reacts aggressively, and walks off despite his father's shout. The headmaster observes but takes no action.

entities.name: Dan Pienaar School Athletics Event
entities.description: A school-organized athletics competition taking place at Dan Pienaar School, involving students in relay races and other sports activities, attended by students, teachers, and staff.
entities.summary: A school-organized athletics competition taking place at Dan Pienaar School, involving students in relay races and other sports activities, attended by students, teachers, and staff.

entities.name: Johan wins the final leg of the relay race
entities.description: Johan, a 15-year-old student, finishes the last leg of a relay race neck-and-neck with a competitor and crosses the finish line just ahead, winning the race for his team.

entities.name: Students and spectators celebrate Johan's race victory
entities.description: After Johan wins the race, students rush onto the sports ground to congratulate him, while his father Ben and teacher Viviers express pride and excitement.

entities.name: Ben du Toit assigns gardening tasks to Gordon Ngubene
entities.description: After the race, Ben du Toit speaks with Gordon Ngubene, a laborer working at the school, and assigns him tasks including weeding marigolds and watering the lawn and flowers.

entities.name: Ben du Toit checks on Jonathan's algebra progress
entities.description: Ben du Toit notices Jonathan, Gordon's son, and asks him about his algebra studies, expressing concern and offering support regarding his academic difficulties.

entities.name: Gordon Ngubene expresses gratitude for Ben du Toit's support
entities.description: Gordon Ngubene affirms to Ben du Toit that his son Jonathan is working hard and that he and his wife Emily are deeply grateful for Ben's financial and academic support.

entities.name: Ben Du Toit
entities.description: A 50-year-old Afrikaans history teacher at Dan Pienaar school, father of Johan, and someone who supports Jonathan financially and academically.
entities.summary: A 50-year-old Afrikaans history teacher and father who supports Jonathan, engaged in conversations with a woman and Colonel Viljoen regarding Gordon Ngubene's detention, vouches for him, and shows emotional distress linked to a legal case involving Emily, known to Stanley and Melanie.

entities.name: Johan
entities.description: A 15-year-old student at Dan Pienaar school and son of Ben du Toit, who wins the final leg of a relay race.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old student at Dan Pienaar school, son of Ben du Toit, wins a relay race; Ben interacts with a sparring partner and observes events involving Jonathan, while a white child is seen playing at the school and laughter is heard during Gordon's lawn mowing.

entities.name: Gordon Ngubene
entities.description: A 47-year-old African laborer working at Dan Pienaar school and father of Jonathan, who expresses gratitude for Ben du Toit's support.
entities.summary: A 47-year-old African laborer and father of Jonathan Ngubene, employed at Dan Pienaar school, died in police detention under investigation; Ben du Toit vouches for his innocence, while Dr. Herzog examined him for toothache and his death is subject to court inquiry.

entities.name: Jonathan
entities.description: A 15-year-old student at Dan Pienaar school and son of Gordon Ngubene, who is studying algebra with support from Ben du Toit.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old student and son of Gordon Ngubene, injured from police caning, is arrested with others outside a beer hall, not selected as a prisoner, and later visits with his father, prompting concern from Ben and Susan.

entities.name: Vivier
entities.description: A young teacher at Dan Pienaar school who cheers for Johan during the relay race.
entities.summary: A young teacher at Dan Pienaar school cheers for Johan, attends a gathering where a guest declines wine, someone follows Ben to the door, another returns to his seat after reassurance, and a man makes a joke about black people leading double lives.

entities.name: Students harass Jonathan and one trips him
entities.description: A group of students laugh and push each other, then deliberately trip Jonathan, causing him to fall to the ground.

entities.name: Jonathan reacts aggressively after being tripped
entities.description: After falling from being tripped, Jonathan jumps up in anger and prepares to attack the boy responsible.

entities.name: Gordon Ngubene calls out to Jonathan to stop
entities.description: Gordon shouts Jonathan's name to intervene when he sees his son about to attack another boy after being tripped.

entities.name: Mrs. Cloete observes the altercation without intervening
entities.description: Headmaster Mrs. Cloete witnesses the incident involving Jonathan and the students but chooses not to take any action.

entities.name: Jonathan storms off toward the school gate in anger
entities.description: After the confrontation, Jonathan, still enraged, walks away abruptly from the scene toward the school gate.

document_metadata.title: 2、EXT. SOWETO BEER HALL - AFTERNOON
document_metadata.summary: Jonathan, Wellington, and other boys are arrested when police intercept them during a chaotic protest escape, despite their protests of innocence.

entities.name: Group of youths enters beer hall to protest drinking
entities.description: A group of about twenty youths enters the beer hall's drinking area with the intent to confront patrons about alcohol consumption and advocate for a boycott.

entities.name: Leader of youth group delivers protest speech to patrons
entities.description: The leader of the youth group addresses the beer hall clients, criticizing them for drinking while their children starve and calling for a boycott of beer halls in the name of revolution.

entities.name: Drunk man with sideburns challenges youth leader's authority
entities.description: A visibly intoxicated man with sideburns stands up with a stick, asserting that children should not speak disrespectfully to their fathers and suggesting the youths need to be beaten.

entities.name: Patrons advance on youths in response to protest
entities.description: The man with sideburns and several other patrons move aggressively toward the group of youths, prompting them to flee.

entities.name: Youths retreat to serving area and begin destroying property
entities.description: The youths run into the serving area, close the doors behind them, and start breaking up the place in response to the patrons' aggression.

document_metadata.title: 9、EXT. SOWETO SCHOOL - SOWETO UPRISING - MORNING
document_metadata.summary: Montage contrasts peaceful white students and a groundsman with sudden gunshots and carnage in Soweto, showing dead, wounded, and stunned reactions from blacks and police amid chaos.

entities.name: Student leader calls for silence at school gathering
entities.description: An 18-year-old boy, identified as a student leader, calls for silence among the students at Orlando Secondary School, and the crowd immediately complies.

entities.name: Students chant slogans against Bantu education and apartheid
entities.description: Following the student leader's speech, the students shout slogans including 'No to Bantu education,' 'No to apartheid,' and 'Freedom Now' in a coordinated demonstration.

entities.description: The students, led by banner carriers and including Jonathan and Wellington, start marching from the school grounds while singing a freedom song, marking the beginning of a protest action.

entities.description: Multiple groups of student marchers, including Jonathan's group, meet at a crossroad to join a larger protest march already in progress.

entities.description: Marching students chant the slogan 'If we learn Afrikaans, Vorster must learn Zulu,' asserting resistance to the imposition of Afrikaans in schools.

entities.description: As they march, students sing freedom songs to maintain unity and express political resistance, continuing throughout the demonstration.

entities.name: Police block march route with jeeps and troop carriers
entities.description: Three police jeeps and troop carriers ('hippos') are positioned to block the path of the student protest march, establishing a physical barrier and military presence ahead of the approaching demonstrators.

entities.name: Police dog handlers confront advancing march
entities.description: Six police dog handlers in camouflage uniforms stand across the road, waiting for the march to approach, with dogs straining at their leashes and handlers taunting the leading students.

entities.name: Soweto police Commandant issues dispersal order via loudspeaker
entities.description: The Soweto police Commandant steps forward with a loudspeaker, confronts the lead of the march, and orders the students to disperse immediately, declaring the demonstration illegal.

entities.name: Students defiantly sing African national anthem Nkosi Sikelele
entities.description: In response to the police order, the students begin singing the African national anthem 'Nkosi Sikelele,' including young children aged 8 to 10 who sing loudly with clenched fists, showing collective defiance.

entities.name: Police prepare for confrontation with tear gas and gas masks
entities.description: Following a command from the Commandant, police carrying tear gas move to the front and begin donning gas masks in preparation for crowd suppression.

entities.name: Crowd chants slogan against Bantu education after Commandant's warning
entities.description: After the Commandant's final warning, a voice in the crowd shouts 'Bantu education...', prompting the crowd to respond in unison with 'Stinks, Stinks, Stinks,' reinforcing their opposition to the education system.

entities.name: Police deploy tear gas and attack with dogs
entities.description: The Commandant gives a hand signal, leading to the launch of tear gas canisters into the student crowd and an attack by police dog handlers, causing immediate chaos and panic.

entities.name: Students panic and flee after police attack
entities.description: Following the deployment of tear gas and dog attacks, students scatter in all directions, with several choking and struggling to breathe due to the gas exposure.

entities.name: Students retaliate by throwing stones at police
entities.description: In response to the police violence, some students begin throwing stones, one of which hits a policeman in the face, leading to him being assisted away by a black officer.

relations.subject: black policeman
relations.object: Students retaliate by throwing stones at police
relations.description: The scene explicitly describes a student throwing a stone that hits a police officer, who is then helped away by a black policeman. The black policeman is not the one hit; however, the relation refers to a police officer (implied as one of the police) being hit. Given the subject is 'black policeman' and the text states 'hitting one in the face; he is helped away by a black policeman', the subject of being hit is a different officer. Therefore, the correct subject should be 'police officer' but since we cannot change the subject, and the black policeman is not the one undergoing the hit, the relation is misaligned. However, the only plausible interpretation is that the black policeman undergoes the event of being targeted or affected by the stone-throwing as part of the police group. But the text does not say he is hit. Thus, no valid rewrite can be made with confidence. Hence, despite initial reasoning, the correct decision is to drop.

relations.description: The tear gas grenades are deployed during the police action, as described in the scene where canisters are thrown into the crowd. This is a transient event tied to a specific moment of action, hence 'momentary'. The grenades are acted upon (deployed) in the event, making 'undergoes' the correct relation type.

His actions and statements reflect a momentary adversarial stance toward the demonstrators' cause, but the text does not establish an enduring hostile relationship with Bantu Education itself—only alignment with enforcing its policy. Thus, 'unfavorable_toward' captures his situational opposition to the protest.

document_metadata.title: 9、EXT. SOWETO SCHOOL - SOWETO UPRISING - MORNING
document_metadata.summary: Montage contrasts peaceful white students and a groundsman with sudden gunshots and carnage in Soweto, showing dead, wounded, and stunned reactions from blacks and police amid chaos.

entities.name: police custody
entities.description: A systemic condition or institutional context in which individuals are held by law enforcement, referenced as the circumstance of Jonathan Ngubene's disappearance.

entities.name: Chris expresses belief that force is the only language certain people understand
entities.description: During dinner, Chris argues that some people are inherently out of control and can only be managed through force, justifying harsh treatment by authorities.

entities.name: Johan challenges Chris by comparing Jonathan Ngubene's age to his own
entities.description: Johan points out that Jonathan Ngubene was only fifteen, the same age as him, and questions whether Chris would apply the same forceful treatment to him.

entities.name: Chris distinguishes Johan from terrorists and justifies violence against them
entities.description: Chris responds to Johan by stating that Johan is not a terrorist, but implies that if he were, he would deserve harsh treatment, reinforcing his support for force against perceived threats.

entities.name: Ben reacts with shock to the reported number of people shot
entities.description: Ben interrupts the conversation upon reading the article, expressing disbelief and moral distress at the report that one hundred people were shot.

entities.name: Susan compares conflicting reports on the number of people shot and blames the media
entities.description: Susan notes discrepancies between the newspaper's claim of one hundred shot and the radio's report of twenty, criticizing the journalist Melanie Bruwer for sensationalism while acknowledging the police were attacked first.

entities.name: Suzette suggests segregation through bantustans to prevent conflict
entities.description: Suzette proposes that separating people into ethnically homogeneous areas, or bantustans, would eliminate social conflict and make everyone happy.

entities.name: Johan questions the labor implications of bantustan policy
entities.description: Johan challenges Suzette's idea by asking who would perform the necessary work if people were segregated into bantustans, highlighting economic dependencies.

entities.name: Susan and Johan begin clearing the dinner table
entities.description: After the conversation, Susan calls on Johan to help clear the dishes, and he stands up to assist, initiating the cleanup process after the meal.

entities.name: Suzette joins Susan and Johan in clearing the table with visible irritation
entities.description: Suzette, showing annoyance, gets up to help clear the dinner table alongside Susan and Johan after the tense discussion.

entities.name: Melanie Bruwer
entities.description: A woman named Melanie Bruwer who reports on the incident involving Jonathan Ngubene, cited as claiming that one hundred people were shot.

document_metadata.title: 35、INT. GORDON'S HOUSE (SOWETO) - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Emily sits motionless in anger as cars drive away; her neighbor Margaret appears at the door after police arrest Gordon and the cleaner.

entities.name: Gordon reads aloud testimony from a handwritten document
entities.description: Gordon reads a detailed account of his and Jonathan's detention and torture at John Vorster Square, describing beatings, interrogation, and a wet bag being placed over his head.

entities.name: Wellington shows signs of paranoia and fear during the reading
entities.description: Wellington becomes increasingly agitated and fearful while listening to Gordon's testimony, nodding and displaying anxious behavior as if expecting an attack.

entities.name: Black cleaner comforts Wellington with a reassuring gesture
entities.description: The black cleaner from John Vorster Square places a sympathetic hand on Wellington's shoulder in response to his visible distress during Gordon's reading.

entities.name: Emily reacts emotionally to Gordon's testimony
entities.description: Emily closes her eyes to block out the disturbing images evoked by Gordon's account of torture and later sobs silently, overwhelmed by grief.

entities.name: Robert silently observes the reading with growing anger
entities.description: Robert stands beside Emily's chair, watching and listening intently to Gordon's testimony, his expression revealing increasing anger at the recounted abuses.

entities.name: Gordon struggles with emotional pain after recounting Jonathan's beating
entities.description: After describing hearing Jonathan being beaten and subsequently disappearing, Gordon falls into a long silence, closes his eyes, and visibly battles with his sorrow.

entities.name: Gordon offers pen for Wellington to sign the statement
entities.description: Gordon presents a pen to Wellington, indicating that he should sign the document at the end of the testimony.

entities.name: Wellington panics at sound of approaching truck and flees through window
entities.description: Upon hearing a truck approach, Wellington rushes to the window, becomes terrified, and abruptly runs into a bedroom and jumps out through the window to escape.

entities.name: Testimony Reading In The Crowded Room
entities.description: A gathering in a small, dimly lit room where Gordon reads a firsthand account of political detention and torture, witnessed by Emily, Robert, Wellington, the black cleaner, and others present.
entities.summary: A gathering in a small, dimly lit room where Gordon reads a firsthand account of political detention and torture, witnessed by Emily, Robert, Wellington, the black cleaner, and others present.

entities.name: small dark room
entities.description: A confined, poorly lit interior space where the group is gathered for the testimony reading.

entities.name: John Vorster Square
entities.description: A detention facility where Gordon and Jonathan were held and interrogated.
entities.summary: Multiple facilities in South Africa, including police stations, detention centers, and government buildings in Johannesburg, are referenced as sites of interrogation, detention, and official inquiries, with historical significance tied to suspicious deaths and confrontations.

entities.name: table
entities.description: A piece of furniture in the room where Gordon and Wellington are seated and the testimony is being read.

entities.name: stove
entities.description: A heat source near which Emily is seated in the room.

entities.name: iron bed
entities.description: A metal bed in the room where the youngsters are sleeping.

entities.name: bedroom
entities.description: A separate room within the dwelling where Wellington flees and jumps through the window.

entities.name: on the second day of our detention
entities.description: A relative temporal anchor indicating when Gordon and Jonathan were taken to the top floor of John Vorster Square for beating.

entities.name: one day
entities.description: A nonspecific but scene-relevant time reference marking when Gordon and Jonathan were interrogated continuously by Capt. Stolz and other policemen.

entities.name: the next day
entities.description: A relative temporal anchor indicating when Gordon learned Jonathan had been taken to hospital.

entities.name: Gordon
entities.description: A man reading aloud a handwritten testimony about his detention and abuse at John Vorster Square, visibly affected by the emotional weight of the memories.
entities.summary: A group of individuals, including Jonathan's visitor, a wronged father, a groundsman, a commuter, a man questioning Jonathan's abduction, and a distressed man at the police station, reflect varied personal and social tensions.

entities.name: Wellington
entities.description: A man exhibiting signs of paranoia and fear during the testimony reading, who ultimately flees upon hearing a truck approach.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old boy, friend of Jonathan Ngubene, participates in a protest, flees but returns to help an injured girl, is arrested, not selected in prisoner screening, held in a cell, and hears abuse in an interrogation room.

entities.name: Emily Ngubene
entities.description: A woman present during the testimony reading who reacts emotionally, closing her eyes and sobbing in response to the recounted violence.
entities.summary: A grieving woman, wife of Gordon, is depicted in moments of distress and relief, comforting her child, reacting emotionally to violence, identifying her children's bodies, and tending a garden, while participating in a group seeking help.

entities.name: Robert
entities.description: A man standing beside Emily who silently observes the reading with growing anger.
entities.summary: Multiple individuals are described in relation to Gordon, Emily, and Margaret, including family members and interactions marked by tension, grief, and silent observation during various emotional scenes.

entities.name: black cleaner from John Vorster Square
entities.description: A cleaner of African descent who comforts Wellington with a reassuring gesture during the testimony reading.

entities.name: Jonathan
entities.description: A person mentioned in Gordon's testimony who was detained and severely beaten alongside him, later taken to hospital and never seen again.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old student and son of Gordon Ngubene, injured from police caning, is arrested with others outside a beer hall, not selected as a prisoner, and later visits with his father, prompting concern from Ben and Susan.

entities.name: Capt. Stolz
entities.description: A police captain who interrogated and physically abused Gordon and Jonathan during their detention at John Vorster Square.
entities.summary: A police captain involved in the interrogation and abuse of Gordon and Jonathan at John Vorster Square also intercepts Suzette Klopper to spare her a trip to the office and is seen conversing with Cloete upon arriving at the building.

entities.name: Ngubene
entities.description: A name shouted by Capt. Stolz during Jonathan's beating, possibly referring to Jonathan or another detainee.

entities.name: Toni Mtimkulu
entities.description: A person sought by Capt. Stolz during interrogation, believed to be associated with a student committee.

entities.name: A.N.C.
entities.description: A political organization that the detainees were accused of working for during interrogation.
entities.summary: An anti-apartheid political organization, banned under apartheid, is suspected by the S.B. of recruiting and collaborating with individuals including Gordon Ngubene, Ben, and Viviers, and is a focus of interrogation and investigation.

entities.name: handwritten document

entities.description: The front door bursts open as five policemen enter, causing the youngest child to wake up suddenly and begin crying.

entities.name: Emily comforts her crying child
entities.description: Emily goes to the bed, picks up her startled child, and returns to her chair to calm him.

entities.name: Captain Stolz arrives and inspects the documents
entities.description: Captain Stolz enters the room, receives the papers from Lieutenant Venter, silently reads them, folds them, and places them in his jacket pocket.

entities.name: Captain Stolz confronts Gordon
entities.description: Captain Stolz orders Gordon to stand and addresses him by name, initiating a tense confrontation.

entities.name: Captain Stolz acknowledges the black cleaner
entities.description: Captain Stolz turns to the black cleaner, implies prior acquaintance, and causes him to stand automatically in response.

entities.summary: Multiple police officers are involved in Gordon Ngubene's arrest and interrogation, with one confiscating documents, another administering electric shocks via a device called 'Samson,' and others present during the arrest and detention.

document_metadata.title: 60、INT. INTERROGATION ROOM (JOHN VORSTER SQUARE) - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Gordon is tortured with electric shocks by Stolz and Venter during interrogation about activists; a letter arrives via Seroke, but no reply is given. Gordon denies A.N.C. involvement and screams under shock.

entities.name: Venter and Johannes restrain Gordon with handcuffs and manacles
entities.description: Lieutenant Venter handcuffs Gordon's wrists while Johannes removes his trousers and underpants and manacles his ankles, fully immobilizing him in preparation for interrogation.

entities.name: Johannes retrieves a rod for interrogation
entities.description: Johannes fetches a metal rod, which is later positioned between Gordon's joints as part of the physical coercion setup.

entities.name: Venter prepares electric wires with electrodes
entities.description: Venter takes two electric wires with electrode attachments from a cupboard and places them on the desk, indicating intent to use electrical torture.

entities.name: Venter and Johannes position the rod on Gordon's body
entities.description: The rod is placed between Gordon's elbow joints and the back of his knees, securing him in a spread-eagle configuration in preparation for torture.

entities.name: Captain Stolz arrives late to the interrogation
entities.description: Captain Stolz enters the room carrying a file, apologizes for his delay, and immediately takes charge of the ongoing interrogation procedure.

entities.name: Johannes adjusts the table to align with the desk
entities.description: At Captain Stolz's instruction, Johannes moves the table into alignment with the desk to facilitate the physical setup for Gordon's torture.

entities.name: Gordon is lifted and secured between desk and table
entities.description: Lieutenant Venter and Johannes lift the restrained Gordon, along with the rod, and position him between the desk and table, fully immobilizing him for interrogation.

entities.description: Captain Stolz grabs Gordon by the head and swings it back and forth in a dehumanizing and disorienting gesture before beginning questioning.

entities.description: Stolz shows Gordon documents from a file, including an affidavit, asserting knowledge of his associates Wellington and others, and demands further names.

entities.description: An activist woman in the next room shouts angrily, escalating her protests during Gordon's interrogation, drawing irritation from Captain Stolz.

entities.name: Captain Stolz orders water for interrogation
entities.description: After muttering about the shouting woman, Captain Stolz commands Johannes to bring water, likely to be used as part of the interrogation or torture process.

entities.description: A structured, coercive interrogation conducted by Captain Stolz, Lieutenant Venter, and Johannes, involving physical restraint, psychological intimidation, and preparation for torture to extract information from Gordon.

document_metadata.title: 61、INT. DUTCH REFORM CHURCH - MORNING
document_metadata.summary: Bester concludes his sermon on Afrikaner resilience and divine purpose as the congregation rises to sing a hymn, with Ben observing his friends and Johan distracted by Cloete's daughter.

entities.name: Dominee Bester delivers a sermon about divine creation and national destiny
entities.description: Dominee Bester preaches from the pulpit, asserting that God created the human race with designated territories and durations for each nation, emphasizing the preservation of creative diversity.

entities.name: Dominee Bester invokes the legacy of the Voortrekkers to inspire cultural preservation
entities.description: Bester draws a parallel between the current congregation and the Voortrekkers, urging the community to uphold the Afrikaner way of life in times of danger by clinging to justice, truth, and ancestral traditions.

entities.name: Church Service Led By Dominee Bester
entities.description: A religious gathering in which Dominee Bester delivers a sermon, with deacons and congregants such as Ben and Cloete in attendance, participating in a structured act of worship.
entities.summary: A religious gathering in which Dominee Bester delivers a sermon, with deacons and congregants such as Ben and Cloete in attendance, participating in a structured act of worship.

entities.name: church
entities.description: The physical setting where Dominee Bester is preaching from the pulpit, implied as the location of the ongoing church service.

entities.name: Ben Du Toit
entities.description: A deacon listening to Dominee Bester's sermon, dressed in black tails and standing with clasped hands during the church service.
entities.summary: An elder family member plays with his grandson Hennie, interacts with Gordon, and participates in activities involving Johan and Jonathan, while expressing concern over Jonathan's treatment by police and reacting to his injuries.

entities.name: Mrs. Cloete
entities.description: A man standing on the opposite side of the church, described as listening in the love of his family during the sermon.
entities.summary: Ben interacts with colleagues and staff who express concerns about his investigations, political involvement, and the school's reputation amid apartheid tensions, while the headmaster and others caution him about professional boundaries and consequences.

entities.name: Afrikanere Way Of Life
entities.description: A cultural and religious identity framed as divinely given and tied to the legacy of the Voortrekkers, emphasized as something to be preserved.
entities.summary: A cultural and religious identity framed as divinely given and tied to the legacy of the Voortrekkers, emphasized as something to be preserved.

entities.name: Voortrekkers
entities.description: Ancestors of the Afrikaner people who migrated into the South African interior, invoked as a symbolic model for cultural preservation and divine mission.
entities.summary: Ancestors of the Afrikaner people who migrated into the South African interior, invoked as a symbolic model for cultural preservation and divine mission.

entities.name: Congregation rises to sing hymn after Dominee Bester's sermon
entities.description: Following Dominee Bester's sermon, the church congregation stands up as the organ begins playing a hymn, and they collectively sing.

entities.name: Johan becomes distracted by Cloete's daughter during church service
entities.description: While the church service is ongoing, Johan sits beside Susan and grows visibly bored, directing his attention toward Cloete's daughter seated at the end of the pew.

entities.name: Suzette
entities.description: A friend of Ben's who is present in the church service and listens intently to the sermon.
entities.summary: Ben and Susan Du Toit's daughter, present at a family dinner and church service, reacts with amusement and concern to Ben's actions, shows off her baby, and participates in discussions involving Gordon's detention and the Rand Daily Mail.

entities.name: Susan
entities.description: A friend of Ben's who is present in the church service and listens intently to the sermon.
entities.summary: Various individuals attend a gathering involving the Du Toit family, interacting with Ben and Johan, serving food, recalling Jonathan Ngubene's past, and connecting with Lewinson and Cloete, reflecting on personal and familial relationships.

entities.name: Johan
entities.description: A friend of Ben's who is present in the church service and becomes visibly bored, distracted by Cloete's daughter.
entities.summary: A 15-year-old student at Dan Pienaar school, son of Ben du Toit, wins a relay race; Ben interacts with a sparring partner and observes events involving Jonathan, while a white child is seen playing at the school and laughter is heard during Gordon's lawn mowing.

entities.name: Cloete's daughter
entities.description: The daughter of Cloete, seated at the end of the pew and noticed by Johan during the church service.

entities.name: organ
entities.description: A musical instrument played during the church service to accompany the congregation's hymn.

relations.description: The suicide note is the entity being presented by Advocate Louw in court, as described in the scene text. The note is actively used in the presentation, making 'performs' appropriate with the predicate 'is presented by' to form a fluent statement: 'Suicide Note is presented by Advocate Louw presents Ngubene's alleged suicide note'. However, this phrasing is awkward due to the object's structure. Despite the syntactic complexity, the action is clearly a single, transient event grounded in the text — Louw physically hands the note to the clerk — justifying a momentary persistence. Given the allowed relations, 'performs' best captures the note's role as the object of presentation, even though the directionality is inverse to typical agent-action framing. Rewriting the relation_type to 'performs' with a reversed predicate ensures schema compliance without inventing information.

document_metadata.summary: Bruwer emphasizes hope and responsibility; Ben expresses gratitude and leaves, comforted by their conversation.

entities.name: Ben arrives at Bruwer's house and searches the garden
entities.description: Ben stops the car in the Bruwer driveway and, from the driver's seat, looks around the garden trying to locate Bruwer.

entities.name: Ben knocks on the front door with no response
entities.description: Ben walks to the front door of Bruwer's house and knocks, but receives no answer.

entities.name: Ben finds Bruwer weeding the vegetable garden
entities.description: Ben goes around to the back of the house and discovers Bruwer kneeling in the garden, weeding among herbs and vegetables.

entities.name: Bruwer identifies the herbs in his garden
entities.description: Bruwer points out various herbs in his garden—thyme, oregano, feunel, sage, and rosemary—and comments on their suboptimal growing conditions.

entities.name: Bruwer invites Ben to taste his greengage wine
entities.description: After discarding his weeding fork, Bruwer invites Ben to sample his homemade greengage wine, claiming to be the only person in the country making it.

entities.name: Bruwer serves greengage wine to Ben
entities.description: Bruwer leads Ben to two old chairs by the back wall, then goes into the kitchen and returns with a bottle of greengage wine and two glasses, which he pours for them.

entities.name: Bruwer reflects on philosophy and abstraction
entities.description: While sipping wine, Bruwer comments on how decades of philosophy have led him back to the earth, criticizing modern life as dominated by harmful abstractions like Hitler, apartheid, and the American Dream.

entities.name: Ben and Bruwer discuss Jesus and misunderstanding
entities.description: Ben brings up Jesus, and Bruwer responds that Jesus was misunderstood, continuing his critique of how ideas are distorted over time.

entities.name: Ben lies about enjoying the greengage wine
entities.description: When asked for his opinion, Ben falsely tells Bruwer that the greengage wine is quite nice, though he appears unenthusiastic.

entities.name: Bruwer acknowledges Ben's difficult path
entities.description: Bruwer tells Ben that Melanie has spoken about him and acknowledges that the path Ben has chosen is not an easy one.

entities.name: Ben expresses feeling of having no choice
entities.description: Ben responds to Bruwer's comment by saying he feels he has no choice in the path he is taking.

entities.name: Bruwer asserts the importance of personal choice
entities.description: Bruwer strongly counters Ben's claim, insisting that one always has a choice, and expresses gratitude that Ben made the choice he did, urging him to stay vigilant.

entities.name: Bruwer passes gas during conversation
entities.description: During the discussion, Bruwer farts loudly, momentarily shocking Ben, but Bruwer continues speaking without pause.

entities.name: Bruwer reflects on Boer heritage and loss of values
entities.description: Bruwer reminds Ben they are both Boers, recalls the hard work of their people to establish themselves in the land, and laments the current state of society as driven by systems rather than spiritual values.

document_metadata.title: 126、INT. BEN'S KITCHEN - AFTERNOON
document_metadata.summary: Stanley confronts the family after a racial slur, tensions escalate, Ben tries to mediate, Chris wants to eject Stanley, and the father-in-law storms out, declaring nothing has changed.

entities.name: Stanley enters the kitchen abruptly in festive attire
entities.description: Stanley bursts into the kitchen wearing a white suit, white shoes, and a scarlet tie, visibly drunk and disrupting the family gathering with his sudden entrance.

entities.name: Stanley greets the family with a loud Christmas salutation
entities.description: After noticing the family, Stanley grins and booms 'Merry Christmas, everyone!' breaking the silence and shocking the Du Toits.

entities.name: Ben rises slowly and approaches Stanley
entities.description: In response to Stanley's arrival, Ben stands up from the table as if in a daze and moves toward Stanley, who recognizes him immediately.

entities.name: Stanley exchanges a tense greeting with Ben
entities.description: Stanley affectionately calls Ben 'Lanie' and offers seasonal greetings, prompting Ben to ask why he is there, creating an atmosphere of unease.

entities.name: Father-in-law confronts Stanley with a racial slur
entities.description: The father-in-law stands, approaches the kitchen, and demands to know who the 'Kaffir' is, referring to Stanley in a derogatory manner.

entities.name: Stanley reacts with shock and challenges the father-in-law
entities.description: Stunned by the insult, Stanley retorts by asking the father-in-law to identify him using the slur 'Boer', escalating the racial tension in the scene.

entities.name: Du Toit Family Christmas Dinner
entities.description: A family gathering hosted by the Du Toits during which Stanley's unexpected and disruptive arrival creates a confrontation.

entities.summary: A black man, friend of Gordon, inquires about a missing person at a police station, interacts with Sergeant Van Zyl, observes identifications, travels in Soweto, and is linked to a pirate taxi driver and events involving Julius and Emily.

entities.description: An older male member of the Du Toit family who confronts Stanley with a racial slur, expressing hostility toward his presence.

entities.description: A large handkerchief, red in color, protruding from Stanley's pocket, matching his tie and contributing to his flamboyant appearance.

entities.name: Father-in-law expresses outrage at being called a Boer
entities.description: The father-in-law reacts with intense anger upon hearing Stanley refer to him as a Boer, interpreting it as a racial provocation.

entities.name: Chris enters the kitchen prepared to confront Stanley
entities.description: Chris rushes into the kitchen upon hearing the escalating argument, ready to physically intervene in defense of the father-in-law.

entities.name: Chris urges Ben to call the police on Stanley
entities.description: After hearing the father-in-law's insult and Stanley's retort, Chris insists that Ben involve law enforcement to remove Stanley from the house.

entities.name: Ben instructs Stanley to wait outside
entities.description: Attempting to de-escalate the situation, Ben tells Stanley to leave the immediate area and wait outside while he handles the conflict.

entities.name: Stanley questions the identity and authority of the family
entities.description: In a state of anger and disbelief, Stanley challenges who the family members are and resists being ordered around in their home.

entities.name: Ben asserts his authority over the household
entities.description: Ben reminds Stanley that despite the tension, the house is still his and he has control over how the situation unfolds.

entities.name: Chris attempts to physically eject Stanley
entities.description: Chris moves aggressively toward Stanley with the intent to throw him out, escalating the confrontation to physical threat.

entities.name: Ben intervenes physically between Chris and Stanley
entities.description: Ben steps in to block Chris from reaching Stanley, pushing Chris back into the dining room to prevent violence.

entities.name: Stanley mocks Chris and invites confrontation
entities.description: Stanley laughs and encourages Chris to try to attack him, showing defiance and provoking further conflict.

entities.name: Ben requests private time with Stanley
entities.description: Ben asks the father-in-law to allow him to speak with Stanley alone, intending to resolve the matter without further interference.

entities.name: Father-in-law declares no change in family dynamics and exits
entities.description: The father-in-law asserts that nothing has changed in the household, then leaves for the dining room, signaling emotional withdrawal.

document_metadata.summary: Ben and Melanie share a tender, intimate moment while dancing, revealing emotional closeness amid their dangerous mission to expose government brutality using affidavits from Zambia.

entities.name: Ben sits on Professor Bruwer's chair while Melanie remains on the settee
entities.description: Ben occupies Professor Bruwer's chair in a tense state, while Melanie stays curled up on the old settee, setting the scene for a serious conversation.

entities.name: Melanie warns Ben about being perceived as a danger
entities.description: Melanie tells Ben that the authorities do not understand his position and see him as a threat, emphasizing the need for caution in navigating their system.

entities.name: Ben requests Melanie's help to expose the security services
entities.description: Ben explains that without Emily, they cannot continue their civil suit and must instead turn to the press to reveal the brutality and power of the security services.

entities.name: Melanie emphasizes the protective power of media exposure
entities.description: Melanie agrees with Ben's plan and adds that going public will not only inform the world but also allow parliamentary scrutiny and public awareness of oppressive laws.

entities.name: Ben realizes the true enemy lies within their own society
entities.description: Ben reflects aloud that the opposition is not located in Soweto but in the internal structures of their society—its bigotry, laws, and systemic injustice.

entities.name: Melanie expresses urgency in winning the internal struggle
entities.description: Melanie responds to Ben’s realization by stating that they must succeed before the Black population achieves victory, underscoring a racialized political tension.

entities.name: Ben and Melanie share a moment of laughter
entities.description: Following their intense exchange about societal conflict, Ben and Melanie briefly laugh together, lightening the mood momentarily.

entities.name: Ben outlines the need for critical affidavits to proceed
entities.description: Ben explains that before approaching the press, he requires two key documents: an affidavit from Dr. Hassiem, who is detained, and one from Wellington, who has fled to Zambia.

entities.name: Melanie offers to travel to Zambia to retrieve the affidavit
entities.description: Upon learning Wellington is in Zambia, Melanie volunteers to go there using her British passport and knowledge of Lusaka to obtain the necessary document.

entities.name: Ben expresses surprise and approval at Melanie's offer
entities.description: Ben reacts with surprise when Melanie proposes going to Zambia, then acknowledges the usefulness of her plan.

entities.name: Melanie jumps off the settee to get drinks
entities.description: Excited by the developing plan, Melanie energetically rises from the settee and offers gin and tonics, moving toward the kitchen.

entities.name: Ben watches Melanie with admiration as she moves through the room
entities.description: As Melanie walks away, Ben observes her with tenderness, focusing on her graceful movements, bare feet, and the sway of her dress.

entities.name: Ben murmurs a warning to Melanie to be careful
entities.description: Emerging from a reflective state, Ben softly calls out to Melanie, cautioning her to take care as she moves about the room.

document_metadata.title: 158、EXT. STREET - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Captain Stolz drives into cafe street, sees Ben crossing, accelerates, hits him, and flees; bystanders gather as Ben lies injured.

entities.name: Captain Stolz accelerates and hits Ben with his car
entities.description: While driving into the cafe street, Captain Stolz sees Ben crossing the road, speeds up, and deliberately strikes him with the vehicle, launching Ben into the air.

entities.name: Captain Stolz flees the scene after hitting Ben
entities.description: Immediately after striking Ben with his car, Captain Stolz speeds away without stopping to assist or check on the victim.

entities.name: Bystanders rush to aid Ben after the hit-and-run
entities.description: Following the collision, people nearby run to Ben's side to help him, showing concern and initiating a spontaneous response to the incident.
